why: Both cite OAI_METHOD_142.md as covering; my extra check (the only sqrt-mod-p code uses a deterministic least-QNR search) adds nothing of substance.

Haiku's 'covered' via the sibling Z1766 pass-1 threshold computation is fair, but it skipped the item's data step; I ran it (Coppersmith-regime (★) fails at 0.04% of p≡1(4) in [10⁶,10⁷]), a routine calibration consistent with s3_lll_lenstra.md.
Same lit check (Bloom's density theorem) and same conclusion; I additionally cite the repo memos that already locate the missing hypothesis (|S| ≥ N^{1−o(1)}), but nothing new.
Haiku skipped as vague; the quantification is easy ((★): ≍p log p candidates, ≍log²p winners vs φ(p−1) primitive roots) and is already in B2_ACROSS_FIELDS M1–M4, so nothing important was lost.
Haiku re-verified the data but did not do the requested proof; the proof is a one-line ultrametric argument and my extra finding (the 4-free (★) sub-family alone fails at 1.5%) is routine.

The cited z52b_pass1_L00 Z0394 is about the quaternion proof of Sun's 1-3-5 conjecture, not a refinement search of ES solutions (the actual 32-predicate coverage is z52b fingerprint variants, uncited), and the search was not run. Running it (16 new predicates, primes ≤10⁶) gave survivors plus a content-2 fact lost by Haiku: no ES solution of 4/n has n | x+y+z, by Tho 2021 (4 ∤ (x+y+z)(1/x+1/y+1/z)).
Haiku skipped as generic; the obvious step (d=1, ℤ[i]) shows the smallest CM slices are empty at p≡1(4)/p≡1(24), the known (I)7 genus condition, so only routine content was lost.

The item did define a numerical check ('check numerically for small p'), so 'skipped' was a process error; doing it reproduces R(p) exactly but only re-derives the known additive-character/genus expansion.
Both read the abstract and conclude the failure is BM, which Bright–Loughran exclude for ES; my repo pointers (MARKOFF_ES.md) add nothing new.

Haiku did the requested partial correlation (−0.22 on 372 primes) and I got the same −0.22 on 4703; my extra step (it vanishes after controlling #small q | p−1) is the RESIDUE_HARDNESS effect already in the repo.
'Pure restatement' is essentially right, but the cheap step does show something: L ≥ p(p+2)/4 always, and the forced partition shape is exactly (★). Minor content.
Same argument (ES conditions are divisor events, not difference-set avoidance); the repo already screens 182 in OAI_DUMP_IMPACT.md.

Haiku did not split by p mod 4 and stopped at p ≤ 1500, so its numbers (min gap 0 at p=7; 51% have y−x ≤ 2) are entirely the p≡3(4) isosceles phenomenon and point the wrong way. At p≡1(4) ≤2·10⁵, min(y−x) ≍ p^{0.75} (never ≤ log²p beyond 5·10⁴) and min(z−y) ≥ p, which refutes the item's lead; there is also an exact Pythagorean lemma for gap-g Type I solutions.
